title: 'Avengers: Endgame Encore' Smashes ₹5 Crore in India Advance Sales, Eyes Re-Release Record
excerpt: A week before release, the Marvel reissue has sold 100,000 advance tickets and is gunning for Baahubali: The Epic's all-time re-release opening record.
body:
• Avengers: Endgame Encore has sold 100,000 tickets worth ₹5 crore in advance sales for its opening weekend in India, a week before its September 25 release.
  • Opening-day sales account for nearly 40,000 tickets, with Chennai's eight available shows already sold out and many centres yet to go on sale.
  • Trade forecasters at Pinkvilla project a ₹5-8 crore nett first day — potentially the biggest opening ever for a re-release in India, Hollywood or otherwise.
  • The all-time re-release opening record stands at around ₹9 crore, set by Baahubali: The Epic; Encore is positioned to challenge it.

Seven years after Avengers: Endgame ended an era, India is treating its return like a new release. Avengers: Endgame Encore, the reissue arriving in cinemas on September 25, has sold 100,000 tickets worth ₹5 crore (about $525,000) in advance sales for its opening weekend — with a week still to go.

The numbers, tracked by Pinkvilla, show healthy momentum beyond the headline. Opening day alone accounts for nearly 40,000 tickets, with demand extending into Saturday and Sunday. Remarkably, the film has achieved this on a limited rollout: it is yet to go on sale in several high-collection screens. Chennai has only eight shows available, and every one of them is sold out. Similar situations exist in other centres, where only a fraction of shows have opened.

A re-release behaving like a premiere

The trajectory is striking. Advance booking opened last week, and within 24 hours the film had sold 15,000 tickets; that doubled to 25,000 within days (worth roughly ₹1.50 crore), hit 45,000 by September 15 per Bollywood Hungama's data, and has now crossed the 1-lakh mark. "A start like this will be considered great for a new release; here, this is a re-release of a seven-year-old film," Pinkvilla noted — and the film has done it with two weeks to spare.

With a week still remaining, the advances would ordinarily point toward a ₹20 crore nett opening day for a fresh release. Because this is a reissue, momentum will not be as strong — but trade forecasters still expect ₹5-8 crore nett on day one, with upside if full inventory goes live and accelerates sales. That would make it the biggest opening for a Hollywood re-release in India, comfortably.

Chasing Baahubali's record

The benchmark is steep. The all-time re-release opening record in India is held by Baahubali: The Epic, the remastered combined edition of both Baahubali films, which collected around ₹9 crore on day one. It is followed by Gabbar Singh (~₹5 crore), then Ghilli, Murari and Sanam Teri Kasam at around ₹4 crore each. Encore should clear the latter group with room to spare; whether it can cross ₹9-10 crore is the industry's open question.

Marvel's India revival

The advance sales are also a referendum on Marvel's standing in India. Endgame was the highest-grossing Hollywood film in India at its 2019 release, before being surpassed by Avatar: The Way of Water and, more recently, Spider-Man: Brand New Day. The brand took a hit in the years between, but the all-time-blockbuster success of Brand New Day and anticipation for Avengers: Doomsday have reinvigorated it.

The re-release is said to link Endgame with Doomsday through additional content — a bridge between the saga's past and its future that gives fans a reason to return to the theatre rather than rewatch at home.
